messages:

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: Temporary QPS uplift for launch + PO timing

Hi Priyom,

Quick note from launch ops — we have a surprise spike predicted for next week tied to a partner integration. Can Redwood temporarily lift our rate limit by ~3x for a 48 hour window while we ramp?

We're willing to sign a short PO. Two questions: 1) Do you offer a one-off rate-lift product or is this treated as overrun billing? 2) If billed as overrun, can you provide a path to convert that overrun to committed credit if we migrate to a higher tier within 30 days?

Also looping procurement for PO queue ETA.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Temporary QPS uplift for launch + PO timing

Tom —

Thanks for the heads up and welcome to the launch club. Short answers up front: we can enable a temporary rate-lift and we typically treat unexpected usage two ways (one-off overrun charge, or convert to committed capacity with retroactive credit if you choose a commit within a short window).

Options I recommend:
- Fast-lift (48 hrs): we can activate a policy that raises the qps ceiling to ~3x for 48 hours. This is billed as overrun at our transient uplift rate.
- Conversion window: if you sign a 3-month committed top-up within 30 days, we can apply up to 60% of the overrun fees as a credit against the new commit (subject to minimums).
- Grace credit: for first-time emergency lifts we can offer a one-time 20% grace credit on the overrun invoice if you submit a PO before our next billing cut.

Next steps for rapid enablement: send the PO draft (procurement@) and confirm the exact uplift start/end windows. From an ops perspective I need a simple spike pattern (peak qps and expected total tokens) — the forecast you attached helps.

Irene, Ben — can you confirm we have headroom on the west-coast cluster and an owner for enabling the temporary policy? Also any compliance notes we should surface to Skyrise before enabling?

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri_yom@redwood.ai
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0198

On Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:02 AM priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
> Priyom —
>
> I can confirm we have capacity headroom on the us-west cluster for a 48 hour surge; Ben, can you coordinate the toggle and monitoring?

Ben — please set up a temporary route with fallback to the next tier model if headroom hits 85% and enable KV-cache warming to reduce peak token cost. Also note: for any overrun conversion we require the customer to provide a signed PO and an audit log export for the uplift window (simple metering file) so Finance/Legal can reconcile before applying credits.

Tom — compliance note: no additional SOC/TLS work required for a short window, but if Skyrise will store customer-sensitive prefixes during the surge please flag it (we may need a data-processing addendum).

Irene Choi
Head of Platform Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@skyrise.ai>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, procurement@skyrise.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Temporary QPS uplift for launch + PO timing

Tom —

We can stand up the transient uplift tomorrow at 09:00 PST. I'll coordinate autoscaling thresholds and set an 85% headroom trigger that will automatically throttle to the fallback model. Monitoring and a metering export will be available as a CSV at the end of the window.

For billing, please send the PO draft to procurement@redwood.ai; our billing team will provision the uplift as an overrun item on your next invoice. To lock in the conversion-credit path (apply 60% of eligible overrun to a new 3-month commit) we need: 1) signed PO for the commit within 30 days, 2) the metering CSV we generate, and 3) a short acceptance email from Skyrise confirming migration intent.

I've attached a PO template and a sample metering CSV layout to make procurement easier.

Best,
Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
